# All critical caps at all deepest points need not cover the mixed set

This is an exact counterexample to a proposed structural implication.
It is not a counterexample to (OC). It applies even when every positive
fiber is strictly convex and every critical cap satisfies the null-
supporting-face regularity used by the unique-contact/parity theorem.

## 1. A two-fiber body and its exact point-depth function

Fix d>=2 and R>r>0. Let B be the closed unit Euclidean ball in R^d and
let kappa_d=|B|. Set

    C={ (z,x): 0<=z<=1, ||x||<=R-(R-r)z }.

This is a compact convex body in R times R^d with nonempty interior:
the norm bound has positive affine right side throughout the interval.
Its induced mixed set has exactly two fibers,

    S=({0} times RB) union ({1} times rB).

Both fibers are full dimensional and strictly convex; q=d and mixed
volume is kappa_d(R^d+r^d).

For every point (j,x) of either fiber, its raw mixed depth is exactly
the ordinary raw depth of x in that one ball. The lower bound follows
because every ambient containing cap retains at least the ordinary
point-depth contribution from its own fiber (a constant trace retains
the whole fiber). For the upper bound choose an attaining ordinary
containing halfspace with nonzero continuous normal u and boundary
through x. Lift it to

    a(z-j)+u.(X-x)>=0.

If j=0, a sufficiently negative finite a excludes the other bounded
fiber strictly; if j=1, a sufficiently positive finite a does so.
This retains exactly the selected own-fiber cap. Thus the equality of
point-depth functions is proved for every source, not only at centers.

An ordinary ball's center has depth exactly half its volume. Every
noncentral point has strictly smaller depth: the through-point plane
perpendicular to its outward radial vector cuts off a strict subset
of the corresponding centered half-ball. The intervening nonempty
open slab has positive volume. Consequently the unique global deepest
mixed point is

    Y=(0,0),      Q=kappa_d R^d/2.

The smaller fiber has strictly smaller maximum kappa_d r^d/2. There
are no omitted global maximizers at fiber boundaries or elsewhere.

## 2. The complete menu of all critical containing halfspaces

Write an arbitrary closed ambient halfspace as

    H(a,u,b)={ (z,x): a z+u.x>=b }, (a,u) nonzero.

It contains Y exactly when b<=0. If u=0 it contains the entire large
fiber, whose volume is 2Q, and hence cannot attain Q. Thus an attaining
halfspace has u nonzero. Its large-ball contribution is at least Q,
with equality only when b=0. Indeed b<0 includes a positive slab beyond
its centered half-ball, or includes the entire ball, and gives a strict
increase. Since the total is Q, the smaller-ball contribution must also
vanish. At b=0 this means

    |rB intersect {u.x>=-a}|=0,

which holds exactly when -a>=r||u||. Equality permits the single
supporting point; strict inequality gives an empty trace. We have
therefore identified ALL depth-attaining containing halfspaces:

    H(a,u,0),      u!=0,      a<=-r||u||.                (1)

Conversely every halfspace in (1) contributes exactly half the large
ball and zero volume from the smaller one, so every such cap really
attains Q. This characterizes the full, unbounded family of minimizing
normals; it is not merely a selected positive circuit.

All these caps have a proper positive own section. Their other trace
is either empty or a singleton. Since d>=2, the singleton has zero
H_(d-1) measure. Thus every cap in the complete menu qualifies for the
proved differentiable strict-contact theorem.

## 3. The exact uncovered region has positive mixed measure

The union of ALL the critical halfspaces (1), restricted to S, is
exactly

    ({0} times RB) union ({1} times boundary(rB)).        (2)

Every large-ball point is in some centered half-ball, which can be
extended using (1). At the smaller fiber, any point in a critical cap
must satisfy

    u.x>=-a>=r||u||.

Cauchy--Schwarz and ||x||<=r force ||x||=r. Conversely any boundary
point x of the smaller ball lies in the critical cap with u=x/r and
a=-r. This proves both inclusions in (2).

Hence the uncovered set is exactly

    {1} times int(rB),

with positive mixed volume kappa_d r^d. Its fraction of the whole
mixed set is r^d/(R^d+r^d), approaching 1/2 as r increases to R while
remaining strictly smaller. The only global deepest point and EVERY
one of its critical caps have been included. No choice of extra critical
caps can repair the failure.

## 4. The same failure in every positive integer dimension

The failure is not tied to n=1. Fix n>=1, d>=2, and parameters R>n eps>0.
Let

    C={ (z,x): z in [0,1]^n,
                   ||x||<=R-eps sum_i z_i }.

It is again a full-dimensional compact convex body, and its integer
base set is exactly P={0,1}^n. Write R_z=R-eps sum_i z_i. Every base
is a cube vertex and can be strictly exposed among the finite set by
an integer-coordinate linear functional. A sufficiently large finite
multiple isolates any prescribed own-fiber continuous cap. The same
argument as Section 1 proves equality between mixed and own ordinary
ball depths at every source.

Only z=0 has radius R. Thus Y=(0,0) is the unique global deepest point,
with raw depth Q=kappa_d R^d/2. The COMPLETE critical menu is

    { (z,x): a.z+u.x>=0 }, u!=0,
    a.z<=-R_z||u|| for every z in P\{0}.                (3)

Necessity follows from the exact Q own contribution and nonnegative
other contributions, as before. Sufficiency follows because (3)
excludes the interior of every other ball. The family is nonempty for
every u: choosing each a_i=-R||u|| satisfies every inequality, since
for a nonzero cube vertex of weight k,

    a.z=-kR||u||<=-(R-k eps)||u||=-R_z||u||.

Thus all nonzero-base fiber interiors remain uncovered by ALL critical
caps at ALL deepest points. The union covers the entire large fiber;
on other fibers it can contain only boundary points, which have zero
d-volume. Its mixed volume is therefore exactly kappa_d R^d. The
uncovered fraction is

    1 - R^d / sum_(z in {0,1}^n) (R-eps sum_i z_i)^d,

which tends to 1-2^(-n) as eps decreases to zero. All radii, and hence
all fiber volumes, can be made arbitrarily close to equal. The exact
equal-radius limit changes the maximizer set and cannot be substituted
for the strict positive eps examples.

The critical menu (3) has only proper own cuts and null supporting or
empty other cuts, so all its members retain the same derivative
regularity for d>=2. This example satisfies the uniqueness and parity
count perfectly while disproving the proposed coverage implication.

## 5. Exact scope of the obstruction

These examples themselves satisfy (OC) by the own-ball contribution;
indeed maxdepth=kappa_d R^d/2 and the largest radius dominates the average
fiber volume. No claim is made that they meet every volume condition
imposed in a hypothetical minimal-counterexample reduction. What fails
is the unrestricted inference from finite/parity-bounded global centers
and differentiable unique contact to coverage of S by their critical
caps. Such coverage would need an additional, separately proved
hypothesis. Volume comparability, strict convexity, complete critical
menus, and actual source-depth maximality do not supply it on their own.

## 6. A stronger three-disk counterexample: strict no-heavy volumes

There is a counterexample preserving strict convexity AND strict
no-heavy volumes. Let T be a centered planar Euclidean disk of area one,
and set

    A=(1/2)T,    K=T,    B=(11/10)T.

Place these fibers at bases -1,0,1. Their convex hull is a full-
dimensional convex body with exactly those integer fibers, because
(A+B)/2=(4/5)T is contained in K. Their areas are

    |A|=1/4,    |K|=1,    |B|=121/100,
    M=123/50,   M/2=123/100.

Every fiber has area STRICTLY smaller than M/2. All are strictly convex.

For any through-origin nonvertical halfspace write its captures as

    A_cap=A intersect {u.x>=alpha},
    K_cap=K intersect {u.x>=0},
    B_cap=B intersect {u.x>=-alpha}.

Here the ambient inequality is u.x+alpha z>=0. Reflection shows

    |A_cap|+|B_cap|
       =|A|+|B_cap outside (-A)|.                       (4)

Indeed B contains -A, and the reflected complement of A_cap is precisely
the cap of -A at threshold -alpha, up to a null cutting line. Moreover
-A is compactly contained in int B. If B_cap has positive area, it has
positive area outside -A: its threshold is below h_B(u), whereas
h_(-A)(u)<h_B(u). The portion above the larger of those two thresholds
is a nonempty proper B cap and lies outside -A. Thus (4) is at least
1/4, and equality holds exactly when B_cap has zero area.

The central disk contributes exactly 1/2 in every through-center
continuous direction. Purely integer containing caps include all of K
and hence have mass at least one. Every containing cap can first be
shifted through the source without increasing its mass. Therefore

    D_S(0,0)=Q=1/4+1/2=3/4.

Equality is attained by every continuous direction with a sufficiently
negative finite alpha, making A strictly full and B strictly empty.
The full list of critical containing halfspaces has boundary through
the source and B_cap of zero area. A cap with a strict containing offset
has strictly larger mass than its parallel through-source shift, because
it adds a positive own-fiber slab. If T has radius rho, the complete
menu is exactly

    {u.x+alpha z>=0},    u!=0,
    alpha<=-(11 rho/10)||u||.                           (5)

The source is the UNIQUE global deepest mixed point. At any other middle
point y, isolate A as full and B as empty while retaining a minimizing
ordinary through-y disk cap. Its mass is 1/4+f_K(y)<3/4. At the two
exposed endpoint bases, finite tilts isolate arbitrary own caps, so
the maximum depths there are their ordinary maxima,

    |A|/2=1/8,      |B|/2=121/200<3/4.

Thus the complete family (5) includes ALL critical caps at ALL global
maximizers. Its union on S is exactly

    ({-1} times A) union ({0} times K)
          union ({1} times boundary B).

A is strictly full in each cap, K is covered as u varies, and a B
boundary point is captured by its tangent member of (5). Every interior
point of B is missed by every member. The uncovered mixed area is
121/100, a fraction 121/246 of the total. Every critical cap has a proper
own section and empty or singleton B trace, so the unique-contact
regularity assumptions hold for the ENTIRE critical menu.

This example refutes coverage even after imposing the strict no-heavy
condition, strictly convex positive fibers, a unique actual global
maximizer, and full differentiability of every critical cap. It still
satisfies OC and makes no contrary claim.

## 7. The same volume tuple with own capture exactly Gamma_2

The root independently supplied a triangle variant retaining the exact
ordinary Gruenbaum constant. Let T instead be any centroid-zero planar
triangle of area one, with the same A,K,B and the same actual three-
fiber convex hull. The areas and strict no-heavy inequalities are
unchanged. If its vertices are v_1,v_2,v_3, their sum is zero and
-v_i=v_j+v_k belongs to 2T. Thus -T is contained in 2T, and

    -A=-(1/2)T subset T subset int((11/10)T)=int B.

The last inclusion follows because the origin is interior and the
homothety factor exceeds one. Identity (4), including its strictness
when B_cap has positive area, therefore remains valid.

Every through-centroid K cap has area at least Gamma_2=4/9. To make the
complete menu explicit without an equality-case citation, evaluate a
nonzero linear functional u at the three vertices. Its values sum to
zero. If the captured side contains exactly one strictly positive
vertex, write these values as p,-q,-r with q,r>=0 and p=q+r>0. Its
triangular cap has relative area

    p^2/[(p+q)(p+r)]
        =1/[(1+s)(2-s)] >=4/9,     s=q/p in [0,1].

Equality holds exactly at s=1/2, so q=r: its cutting line is parallel
to the facet opposite that captured vertex. If the captured side has
two positive vertices, the opposite single-vertex cap has area between
4/9 and 1/2 by the same formula, so the original captured area is at
least 1/2 and cannot be minimal. Zero vertex values are covered by the
end cases and give area 1/2. These cases establish both the bound and
its complete equality classification.

Let lambda_i be the triangle's affine barycentric coordinates and put
ell_i(x)=lambda_i(x)-1/3, a linear functional since the centroid is zero.
The three minimizing continuous directions are exactly the positive
multiples of the ell_i. Thus

    Q=|A|+Gamma_2=1/4+4/9=25/36.

Every critical containing halfspace passes through Y=(0,0), because a
strict containing offset adds positive own mass to its shifted cap.
Pure integer caps have mass at least |K|=1>Q. Equality in (4) and in
the own triangle bound shows that every critical cap has B_cap of zero
area and one of the three canonical continuous directions. Since
max_T ell_i=2/3, its normalized complete menu is

    H_(i,alpha)={ell_i(x)+alpha z>=0},
    i in {1,2,3},     alpha<=-11/15.                    (6)

These and only these halfspaces attain Q. At A, min ell_i=-1/6, so
(6) captures A strictly; at B equality alpha=-11/15 captures precisely
its corresponding vertex, and smaller alpha captures nothing.

Y is again the UNIQUE global maximizer. At another middle point y,
some barycentric coordinate lambda_i(y)>1/3. The cap through y defined
by lambda_i(x)>=lambda_i(y) has area (1-lambda_i(y))^2<4/9. A finite
integer tilt makes A full and B empty without changing that own cap,
proving depth strictly below Q. At the exposed endpoints the complete
point-depth functions equal their own ordinary depths, as before.
Their maximum values are

    Gamma_2 |A|=1/9,
    Gamma_2 |B|=121/225<25/36.

No other fiber or source can attain Q. The union of all critical caps
(6), restricted to S, is exactly A at base -1, all of K at base 0,
and the THREE VERTICES of B at base 1. The K assertion follows because
every point has at least one barycentric coordinate >=1/3. Thus the
entire B interior, of area 121/100, remains uncovered despite ALL
critical caps at ALL deepest sources having been included.

Although the triangle fibers are not strictly convex, every cap in
(6) is proper on K, strictly full on A, and either empty or supported
at a SINGLE VERTEX of B. Its supporting trace is H_1-null. Thus every
one of these critical caps still satisfies the differentiable strict-
contact hypotheses. This variant additionally has the exact own-cap
fraction Gamma_2 in the complete critical menu.
